native_modes.0: Wrong-map finished notification after SQL creates Player but before100ms completion preserves its pending GUID and queues no packets. The valid login still completes.
native_modes.1: A valid early completion records the current map. Wrong-map showing and finished notifications retain that marker and current login/map/socket state; native map admission succeeds.

native_modes.3: Actual far TeleportTo retains the source Player map while the session targets its destination. A source finished notification and unrelated negative-map showing are rejected before the early destination finish; the actual WorldPortAck reaches the destination.
native_modes.4: A valid destination finish before WorldPortAck survives delayed source showing/finished packets. The native far ACK retains that early acknowledgement and completes in the destination.
native_modes.5: Actual far ACK without an early finish completes first. Source-map notifications after arrival queue nothing and do not alter state; a valid destination completion still sends its native initial packets.
native_modes.6: Actual same-map TeleportTo plus HandleMoveTeleportAck completes a40-yard near transfer. Matching-map screen events remain accepted; wrong/negative-map events before and after the movement ACK remain harmless.

limitations_and_pending_client_checks: No WoW client was operated. Loading UI, streamed geometry readiness, movement release, camera, pet portrait and quest traversal remain client checks. Native WMO collision and extracted arrival tests do not verify rendering.

The packet probe observes production serialization/enqueueing on native sockets. It does not pump encryption/network writes or prove client receipt. Fixture enum eligibility and instance type are seeded rather than executing a complete authentication/HMAC exchange.

MapID and Showing contain no request/transfer generation. A delayed packet for the same map as a newer transfer cannot be distinguished by this fix. Matching-map duplicate notifications retain existing behavior; this change rejects different-map events only.

A legitimate early destination completion retains the existing initial-packet dispatch order before WorldPortAck, when Player still belongs to the source. This audit verifies its accepted state/acknowledgement and eventual native transfer; it does not establish that every packet in that pre-existing order carries destination context.

Tests make callback ordering deterministic and stop fixture map workers. They do not prove arbitrary concurrent IO/map/world interleavings. Arrival-grace controls use actual lifecycle methods without claiming a supporting collision object for that specific fixture location.

Character/auth schemas are schema-only scratch databases. Personal account/character rows are not copied or modified, world data is read-only during native execution, and the standalone portal migration check uses connection-local temporary tables.
